result.title: Answer It or Not? Towards Prompt-Adapted Adversarial Images on Vision Language Models
result.summary: With the advancement in language modeling, research on adversarial images has recently shifted from image classifiers to vision-language models (VLMs). Despite the new, text-prompt-driven nature of VLMs, we find that existing VLM adversaries have largely overlooked the dynamics of text prompts. In a typical use case, adversarial images can protect visual privacy by rejecting VLMs from answering questions about the image. However, existing protections are prompt-agnostic, i.e., indiscriminately rejecting any question, including those for potential legitimate use of the image. To address this limitation, we propose Prompt-Adapted (ProAda) adversarial images, which are optimized to balance the rejection of harmful prompts and the correct response of legitimate prompts. In particular, to achieve a more accurate adversarial direction, the text prompt is also iteratively updated with a simple classifier judging whether the harmfulness of the prompt remains. Extensive experiments on visual-privacy-related datasets validate that ProAda can reject over 90% of harmful prompts while allowing over 90% of legitimate ones, demonstrating superior overall performance compared to existing prompt-agnostic VLM adversaries. In addition, our ProAda achieves competitive overall cross-model transferability and improved robustness against countermeasures.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ProAda 提示自适应对抗图像：通过迭代更新文本提示并用简单分类器判断提示有害性是否仍成立，以更准确的对抗方向优化扰动，使 VLM 拒绝有害提问同时仍能正确回答合法提问，在视觉隐私数据集上实现双向超过 90% 的成功率并具备跨模型迁移性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「提示条件化的对抗扰动—拒绝/回答」范式可能充当探针，用于核查 VLM 答案是否真正依赖视觉证据、即视觉旁路问题，并可启发对提示依赖与证据筛选的评测设计，但与原论文的 latent 状态生成机制是否有实质关联尚待核查。
